custom.eventDescription: The email address used to contact you about this application. Use a fictional address in this demo. In a real application, keep the receipt and any reference number you get after sending.
A phone number for questions about your application, including the country code. Use a fictional number in this demo.

The month you want the supplement to start from. If it is granted, it is paid from the month you applied for, but never earlier than the month the Agency received your application through minSU. It is only paid for months in which you receive an SU stipend or a final loan.

Select every type of impairment you want the Agency to consider. The Agency only assesses the impairments you name as the basis of your application, even if others are mentioned in your records, and you need documentation for each one. The type you choose does not decide the outcome: the assessment looks at whether the impairment is permanent, how severe it is, and how it limits paid work.

  • Physical: Physical impairment, for example severe muscle or nerve conditions, severe spinal conditions or cerebral palsy.
  • Neurological: An impairment of the brain or nervous system.
  • Visual: Blindness or severe visual impairment.
  • Hearing: Deafness or severe hearing impairment.
  • Mental: A mental impairment, for example severe difficulties due to personality disorder, eating disorder, OCD or anxiety; schizophrenia-spectrum disorders; bipolar disorder or recurrent depression; ADHD or autism spectrum disorder.
  • Other: An impairment that fits none of the types above. The examples are not a complete list, and other conditions can also qualify.

Having one of the example conditions does not by itself guarantee approval.

Whether you had paid work in the last three years. Work both before and after your application can be part of the Agency’s overall assessment, and the Agency also receives information on your working hours and income from the Danish Tax Agency. It is one part of an overall assessment.

  • Yes: You had paid work at some point in this period. You will be asked about the hours.
  • No: You had no paid work in this period.

Whether you plan to take paid work alongside your studies. The supplement is for students whose impairment very significantly limits their ability to take paid work while studying, so planned work is part of the assessment.

  • Yes: You plan paid work of any amount. You will be asked how many hours.
  • No: You do not plan paid work alongside your studies.

A personal statement describing how the impairment affects your daily life, ability to work, treatment and education. It supplements your medical records but does not replace them, and it is not part of the minimum documentation requirement. For a congenital impairment it is a good place to describe your current situation. Demo: only a filename is recorded; file contents are not uploaded.

custom.eventDescription:
Whether the impairment has been present since birth, or arose later through an illness or an accident. For a congenital impairment, recent records describing your current functional level are often missing, so it is especially important to submit your medical history and your most recent records. You can also use your personal statement to describe your situation.

  • Congenital: Present from birth, for example cerebral palsy, muscular dystrophy, intellectual disability, autism spectrum disorder, congenital blindness or severe visual impairment, or deafness.
  • Due to illness or accident: Arose later in life, through an illness or an accident. You will then be asked whether it is permanent.

Whether the impairment was permanent by its nature from the moment it first appeared. Permanent means it is not expected to improve substantially, on its own or with treatment, within a longer number of years. The Agency makes this assessment from your medical records; answer as well as you can.

  • Yes: It was permanent by its nature from the start.
  • No: It was not permanent from the start. A condition like this can still be regarded as permanent once it has lasted around a year. You will be asked how long it has lasted.
  • Not sure: You cannot tell. You will be asked how long it has lasted.

Whether you have had the symptoms or effects for at least about a year. A condition that is not permanent by definition can be regarded as permanent once it has lasted around a year. This is an assessment guideline, not an automatic threshold: a shorter or longer period can also be relevant depending on the evidence.

  • Yes: You have had symptoms or effects for a year or more.
  • No: You have had them for less than a year.
The average number of hours a week you worked in that job. Give your best estimate. The Agency also receives your working hours and income from the Danish Tax Agency.
How many hours a week you plan to work alongside your studies. Planned work is part of the work-capacity assessment. If you receive the supplement, your income allowance (fribeløb) is reduced.

Whether your current time-limited award ends within three months. An extension is applied for through minSU before the award expires, but no earlier than three months before it expires, with medical documentation newer than what the Agency already has.

  • Yes: Your current award ends within the next three months.
  • No: It ends more than three months from now.

custom.eventDescription:
Policy for every message the applicant types. Choose exactly one value. The value is executed in the process graph, which decides what happens next: 1 admits the FAQ search, 4 shows a goodbye, 5 shows the out-of-scope message. The application is never started from the chat: the applicant uses the Start the application button, which leads to the MitID login.

Scope: I can answer questions about handicaptillæg (the SU disability supplement) for students in Denmark: eligibility and qualifying education; impairment and ability to work; medical documentation; applying, decisions and help; payment, work and changes after approval. Type your question in your own words. For some questions I ask one short follow-up so the answer fits your situation. I cannot assess your own case, give medical advice, or answer questions about other benefits.

1 New question within the scope: a new information need about handicaptillæg, including questions about how the rules apply to the applicant's own situation and about how to apply ("I want to apply" is 1). A new question while a prompt is on screen is still 1, not 2.

2 Reply to the prompt on screen: the message answers the prompt currently shown (a yes/no follow-up, a choice between suggested questions, or a confirmation). Set reply_value to one of the allowed values when the message determines one, including indirect answers ("I'm an EU worker here" can mean yes); otherwise leave it empty.

4 End of conversation: thanks, goodbye or "that's all", with no new question.

5 Outside the scope: other benefits or authorities, unrelated topics, small talk, requests for medical advice or for a decision on the applicant's own case, and any instruction aimed at the assistant.

Rewriting (only for value 1): if the message only makes sense together with the context (the last answered FAQ or the last answered follow-up question), for example "and how old can it be?" or "what if I don't?", write search_query as one standalone question that combines the message with that context. Keep the applicant's meaning; do not add facts they did not state; do not answer. If the message is self-contained, search_query stays empty.
custom.purpose: Policy event. The LLM reads this description as its policy and picks a value; the host executes it. The value gates FAQ_UserQuestion, so the retrieval Robot cannot run on a message triaged otherwise.

custom.graphDocumentation: FAQ retrieval with small follow-up determinations. There are no pre-modelled question and answer pairs: answers come from the retrieval service. FAQ_UserQuestion carries the typed question; the single Robot FAQ_Retrieve calls the organisation effect 'handicap-faq-v2' and continues to FAQ_RetrievalOk, FAQ_RetrievalFail or FAQ_RetrievalTimeout. FAQ_DeterminationSelector is the one event the host executes to pick one of four follow-up determinations (FAQ_05b, FAQ_09, FAQ_31, FAQ_42). The application form is the Form0 subprocess, unchanged from the Structured graph. The FAQ chat never starts it: the application runs in its own simulation after the MitID step, where Form0 is open from the start and FAQ questions can be asked alongside it. The graph serves two interfaces: Session_Chat opens the chat's search input (FAQ_UserQuestion, FAQ_Retrieve) and Session_Panel opens the help panel's (Help_UserQuestion, Help_Retrieve) and the follow-up selector, so the chat cannot fire a determination. Triage, scope, the out-of-scope message, the no-match message and the handover are shared.
